messages:
anna (customer): Hey team, trying to install the private agent in our VPC and the installer fails when pulling model shards + telemetry. Installer log shows TLS verify errors and a 403 on the model shard URL. Can you confirm minimal outbound hosts/ports we need to allow so this can run behind our egress firewall?

maria (support): Sorry you're blocked — we can help. Can you paste the exact installer error / curl output for one of the failing URLs? Also let us know if you have TLS intercept (proxy) in path.

anna (customer): Here's the curl we ran from the node (we're on a locked-down subnet behind corporate proxy):
```
curl -v https://models-cdn.redwood.ai/shards/abc123 -o /dev/null
* Rebuilt URL to: https://models-cdn.redwood.ai/shards/abc123
*   Trying 54.230.12.45...
* Connected to models-cdn.redwood.ai (54.230.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* SSL: certificate subject name (CN) did not match target host name 'models-cdn.redwood.ai'
* Closing connection 0
* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches
* stopped the pause stream!
curl: (60) SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches
```
We also see repeated 403s from the installer when it tries to hit registry.redwood.ai for model metadata.

maria (support): Two things stand out: 1) SNI/certificate mismatch (often caused by TLS MITM/transparent proxy or split-horizon DNS) 2) 403s could be blocked token exchange or blocked auth host. Are you using a corporate HTTPS proxy that does certificate re-signing?

raj (onprem-eng): For our private deploys the minimal outbound hosts we ask customers to allow (HTTPS 443 unless noted):
- auth.redwood.ai (token exchange / auth)
- registry.redwood.ai (model metadata / manifest)
- models-cdn.redwood.ai (model shards, backed by S3/CloudFront)
- telemetry.redwood.ai (usage & health pings)
- pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org (pip packages during bootstrap)
- docker.io, gcr.io, quay.io (if pulling images)
- ocsp.digicert.com and ocsp.globalsign.com (OCSP stapling / certificate validation)
- crl3.digicert.com (CRL fetch may be required in some environments)
- kms.<cloud-provider>.amazonaws.com (if you're using KMS-backed keywrap)
- time servers (ntp) or allow outbound ntp/123 to keep clocks in sync
Also allow UDP/53 (DNS) outbound and ICMP for some installers.

kyle (infra): +1 on DNS and OCSP. If you're doing TLS interception (Zscaler/BlueCoat), make sure the proxy provides SNI passthrough or you add an exception for the hostnames above. Transparent MITM will present the proxy cert and the installer/curl will fail unless the proxy CA is installed on the node.

anna (customer): We do have Zscaler and strict egress IPs only. Our security team doesn't want wide domain rules, they asked for IP ranges. Any advice on IPs?

cara (security): We prefer domain-based allowlisting but understand IP-only rules happen. For CDNs (CloudFront/Cloudflare) the IP ranges are huge and dynamic — recommend whitelist by FQDN on the proxy or use a TLS SNI exception. If IPs are required, we can provide the AWS/CloudFront IP range JSON and the GCP ranges for gcr.io — be aware you'll need updates when ranges change.

maria (support): Practical options: 1) Add SNI passthrough / proxy exceptions for auth.redwood.ai, registry.redwood.ai, models-cdn.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai and pypi.org (recommended), OR 2) Temporarily open outbound 443 to those domains' IPs (use cloud vendor JSON feeds) during install.

raj (onprem-eng): Quick repro command we can run from your node if you can open a tunneled port to us:
```
curl -H 'Accept: application/json' -v "https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/token"
curl -v "https://registry.redwood.ai/v1/models/XYZ/manifest"
curl -I "https://models-cdn.redwood.ai/shards/abc123"
```
If the first call returns a 4xx that indicates token exchange is getting blocked; if the second returns 403 but the first succeeds then registry->model-permission may be the issue.

anna (customer): We ran the three curls behind our proxy — first call returns a 502 from the proxy, second/third return the TLS cert mismatch like above. I can request a proxy exception for the three FQDNs.

maria (support): That should unblock you. Also tell your proxy team to allow connections to ocsp.digicert.com and ocsp.globalsign.com (443) and files.pythonhosted.org (443) so pip installs don't fail.

kyle (infra): Extra note: if you host an internal artifactory instead of hitting pypi, allowlist your artifactory host and files.pythonhosted.org only if you fallback to public pypi. Also ensure the node has the org CA cert (if proxy re-signs).

anna (customer): I'll request SNI exceptions and the OCSP hosts. Can you send a concise checklist I can hand to security?

maria (support): Yep — copy/paste checklist for your security team:
- Allow HTTPS (443) outbound to: auth.redwood.ai, registry.redwood.ai, models-cdn.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org
- Allow OCSP/CRL: ocsp.digicert.com, ocsp.globalsign.com, crl3.digicert.com (443)
- Allow outbound DNS (UDP 53) and ensure split-horizon DNS resolves the public FQDNs to public CDNs (no internal interception)
- If IP-only policy: whitelist AWS CloudFront IP ranges and your cloud provider ranges used for storage/CDN (note: dynamic, needs periodic updates)
- Ensure proxy does SNI passthrough or install corporate CA into node trust store if you must re-sign TLS
- Allow outbound NTP (UDP 123) or ensure node clock is within 5s of real time

maria (support): If they make the changes and you still hit 403, ping me and we can open a short support window to hit a diagnostic endpoint and collect the failing requests. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment trigger queued for diagnostic run (id: diag-2479991234).

anna (customer): Thanks, initiating exception request now. I'll report back after security approves.

maria (support): Great — standing by. If you want we can also provide a temporary pre-signed shard URL to test without auth while your security team makes changes.
